analysis:
Jalayagnam was the flagship irrigation programme of the YSR government, launched in 2004. It comprised 86 projects with an approved cost of about Rs 1.86 lakh crore; 74 projects were sanctioned between 2004-05 and 2008-09. The stated objective was to create a new ayacut of 97.46 lakh acres and stabilise 22.53 lakh acres, mainly in the drought-prone Telangana and Rayalaseema regions.

CAG's performance audit (Report No. 2 of 2012) reviewed implementation of the programme as a whole and of individual projects. It recorded that several projects were taken up without adequate planning and without clearances from agencies including the Central Water Commission, Planning Commission and Ministry of Environment and Forests, and that works did not achieve the objective of providing irrigation to the intended agricultural land.

By the end of YSR's term in 2009 a large share of the targeted new irrigation potential had not been realised, and spending continued well beyond the term. Press reporting in 2013 recorded that about Rs 80,000 crore had been spent on the programme as of March 2012.
notes: The deadline is set to the end of YSR's term (2009); the projects ran well past that date. The exact month of the launch is not asserted here; date is set to 2004-06-01 with the year established by the CAG and MANAGE documents.
